stories.headline: Mayor's April county update on storms, housing and grants
stories.summary: The mayor reviews storm recovery, tsunami and emergency preparedness, housing goals, grant programs, the Wailuku Film Festival and summer program hiring.
stories.text: Aloha mai kākou. Welcome to your April County of Maui update. Our community has been through We've been through a lot navigating three significant weather events over the past few weeks. County crews continue cleanup, debris removal, damage assessment, and repairs across Maui County. Mahalo to everyone who stepped up to kōkua those in need and supported one another through this challenging time. In response, our Office of Recovery has launched Storm Relief Resources online at mauirecovers.org To help residents navigate recovery. Residents can report damage and access support for debris cleanup and other available resources. We have also held community meetings in some of our more heavily impacted areas, including upcountry, Iao Valley, and South Maui. We will continue that outreach on Molokaʻi with a community meeting on April 19th and are working to confirm a date for Hāna. April is Tsunami Awareness Month and these recent storms are a reminder that emergencies can happen at any time, often with little warning. Sign up for Genesis Protect Alerts for real-time updates, know your evacuation zone, and have a plan for your household. Prepare a go-bag with at least three days of food, water, medications, and essential supplies in case you need to evacuate. We also encourage everyone to be two weeks ready at home with enough food, water, and basic supplies to support your household during an emergency or extended power outage. You can sign up for MIMA alerts and find preparedness resources at maui-county.gov-slash-mima. Last month I delivered my fourth State of the County address where I shared the progress we're making and the priorities guiding our work ahead. Housing remains our top priority Because it directly impacts whether local families can continue to live here in Maui County. We are on track to deliver nearly 3,000 affordable and workforce homes by 2030. We are expanding housing opportunities on county-owned land through our experimental and demonstration housing program, partnering with non-profit developers to test innovative and cost-effective building approaches. Applications are open through April 30 at maui-county.gov slash housing. We continue to support recovery efforts through the Hoʻokumuho program with seven housing projects and 21 infrastructure projects moving forward to help restore 519 affordable rental units and rebuild critical systems across our communities. Another county updates the Office of Economic Development's Fiscal Year 2027 Grant Program is open through April 30th. Non-profits and businesses in agriculture, technology, creative industries, and workforce development are encouraged to apply at maui-county.gov. The County of Maui through the Maui Film Office is supporting the inaugural Wailuku Film Festival, taking place June 17th through 21st in Wailuku. Tickets go on sale May 27th at wailukufilm.com. The Department of Parks and Recreation is hiring for the Palo Summer Program running June 8th to July 24th. Apply at governmentjobs.com. In closing, mahalo for your continued trust, patience, and kōkua in keeping one another safe. We remain committed to doing everything we can to support, uplift, and protect our community. Aloha.

stories.text: Maui's ongoing housing shortage is driving urgent demand for all housing projects, but there's a special need for accessible and supportive housing options for the disabled. Laʻakea Villages' proposed housing development in Pahia would add 22 affordable rental homes including dedicated housing for adults with disabilities. Community members can continue to support this project by submitting written testimony to advocate for funding.
